faq-anomaly-body1: If you see an inexplicable spike in pageviews, especially if it is only on specific days, it may be false traffic from an automated program. One tactic to identify bot-inflated traffic is to compare desktop views with mobile views. First see which agents are most popular on your project for all articles, and use that as a basis for comparison. For instance on the English Wikipedia mobile web views should be comparable if not higher than desktop, so if mobile web views are very low, it might be false traffic.
faq-anomaly-body2: If you are unable to conclude it is false traffic, you can request an investigation to be done by filing a ticket on $1. These pageviews anomalies are common and tedious to investigate, so do not expect a timely response.
faq-anomaly-title: Why do some pages have unusually high pageviews?
faq-bug-report-body: If you would like to use a wiki to provide feedback, use the feedback forum on Meta. You can also report issues on Phabricator.
faq-bug-report-title: I have a feature request or bug to report
faq-chart-types-body: Click "$1" to choose amongst 6 different types. The app will remember your preference. By default, the application will show a line chart. Note that the pie, doughnut and polar area charts can only show data for the total number of views within the daterange.
faq-chart-type-title: How can I change the chart type?
faq-counts-body: Yes. Every time you load a page, a pageview is registered, even if you created the page. You can learn more about the pageview definition at $1.
faq-counts-title: Are pageviews by the same user counted every time?
faq-data-dumps: Can I download the full pageviews dataset for all pages?
faq-data-dumps-body: Yes. The full data dumps for all supported Wikimedia sites can be downloaded at $1.
faq-date-dot: What are the dots next to the date labels?
faq-date-dot-body: This indicates the first day of the week. Pageviews tend to be low during the weekends, so this indicator can give perspective to the seven-day pattern.
faq-location-body: The geographic location of readers on a per-page basis is not available. This is primarily for privacy reasons. You can however see the total pageviews by country across all Wikimedia sites at $1.
faq-location-title: Can I see what geographical region the pageviews came from?

faq-massviews-subject-page-body: This option is for when you are using a category as the source. In some cases the category may contain talk pages when you actually want the subject pages. For instance FA-Class New York City articles, which lists the talk pages of FA-quality articles within WikiProject New York City.
faq-multi-lang-title: I want to see data for a page across all languages of a project
faq-editor-types-anonymous: are edits made by users who are not logged in.
faq-editor-types-group-bot: are accounts that are members of the wiki's bot user group — officially flagged bots.
faq-editor-types-name-bot: are accounts that are not in the bot group but whose username identifies them as a bot.

faq-old-data-body: The Wikimedia pageviews API was introduced in August 2015 and has backfilled data to July 2015. You will have to rely on other tools to view data older than this. Whether or not they work is unfortunately outside the scope of this Pageviews Analysis, and beyond the control of its maintainers.
faq-old-data-title: Why can't I view data older than July 2015?
faq-redirects-body: If a user browses to a redirect, a pageview is registered for the redirect but not for the target page. If you want to get the total pageviews of a page including all redirects, enable the "$2" option, or use $1.
faq-redirects-body2: Note the "$1" option can potentially slow down the tool, and edits made to redirect pages are not counted.
faq-referrals-body: Limited referral data for selected Wikipedias is published under a dataset called $1. This data can be explored at $2.
faq-referrals-title: Can I see how readers got to the page?
faq-search-redirects-body: To enable searching for redirects, change your search method to "$1" in the $2 panel. If you want to see the pageviews of individual redirects to a page, try $3.
faq-search-redirects-title: How can I see the pageviews of redirects?
faq-page-types-content: counts only pages in the wiki's content namespaces, such as articles on Wikipedia.
faq-page-types-non-content: counts pages in every other namespace, such as talk, user and project pages.
faq-source-pagecounts: refers to the older, and less reliable way counting pageviews. This data is available from December 2007 to August 2016.
faq-source-pageviews: is the total number of pageviews the project received.
faq-source-unique-devices: is the number of unique devices that visited the site.
faq-todays-date-body: The Wikimedia pageviews API generally takes a full 24 hours to populate, sometimes longer. In some situations you may see data missing for yesterday's date as well, which will be left blank rather than showing a count of zero views.
faq-todays-date-title: Why can't I view data for today's date?
faq-top-viewed-title: I want to see the top viewed pages within a date range
faq-topviews-false-positive-body1: These are false positives, and unfortunately they are unavoidable. These could surface because someone used an automated program to scrape the page, for instance. One tactic to identify false positives is to compare desktop views with mobile views. First see which agents are most popular on your project for all articles, and use that as a basis for comparison for pages you believe may be false positives. For instance on the English Wikipedia mobile web views should be comparable if not higher than desktop, so if mobile web views are very low, it might be a false positive.
faq-topviews-false-positive-body2: You can also open any page in the Pageviews app for further analysis. Just click on the view count on the right side.
faq-topviews-false-positive-body4: You can easily compare mobile and desktop pageviews by checking the "$1" option. This option is only available if you set the $2 to "$3". The percentages include mobile app and mobile web pageviews.
faq-topviews-false-positive-title: Why do some random pages have such high view counts?
